target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (Fm S₀ S : Type) [LogicalConnective Fm] [LogicalNeutral Fm] [Entailment S₀ Fm] [Entailment S Fm]
    (𝓑 : S₀) (𝓢 : S) [Entailment.Cl 𝓑] [Entailment.Cl 𝓢] (K : Fm → Fm),
    Def1 𝓑 𝓢 K → Def2 𝓢 K → Def3 𝓢 K → Def4 𝓢 K →
    ∀ p : Fm, 𝓢 ⊢ ∼K (K (∼p) 🡘 p)

divergences.description: Target omits and cannot express Reinhardt's schema ∃e K ∀x (K φ ↔ x ∈ W_e), the Turing-machine / r.e. predicate W_e, arithmetic, the free-variable condition FV(φ) ⊆ {x}, and the source's claim in [P-A4] that a particular instance of Reinhardt's schema is inconsistent with epistemic arithmetic. Instead, Target states a purely propositional modal schema (∀ p : Fm, 𝓢 ⊢ ∼K (K (∼p) 🡘 p)) that establishes nothing formally about Reinhardt's schema, Turing machines, or computability.

Target omits and cannot express the quantified epistemic logic and diagonalization steps needed to connect the chosen instance ∃e K ∀x (K(x ∉ W_x) ↔ x ∈ W_e) to K(K(∼p) ↔ p)—namely existential elimination on e, universal instantiation x := e inside the scope of the intensional operator K, and necessitation applied to open formulas (moreover, p := 'e ∈ W_e' is an open formula rather than a closed sentence, whereas the setting describes Fm as sentences). Because the entire bridge from Reinhardt's schema to K(K(∼p) ↔ p) remains unformalized, Lean establishes only a propositional modal refutation rather than the inconsistency of an instance of Reinhardt's schema with EA.

Target generalizes from Epistemic Arithmetic (EA) to arbitrary abstract classical propositional systems 𝓑 and 𝓢 with an operator K satisfying Def1–Def4, omitting arithmetic axioms, S4 positive introspection (K φ → KK φ), and full necessitation for 𝓢 while stating Def4 (K(K φ → φ)) explicitly. Because EA satisfies Def1–Def4 (and Def1 with Def3 implies that 𝓢 extends 𝓑), this is a harmless strengthening.

Target formalizes the propositional tail of a specific author-supplied instance (φ := 'x ∉ W_x') yielding K(K(∼p) ↔ p), whereas [P-A4] states only that Reinhardt found some inconsistent instance without specifying which instance or this propositional form.

Relative to [P-A1]'s remark that proofs always involve known factivity K(K φ → φ), Target takes Def4 only as a sufficient hypothesis for refuting K(K(∼p) ↔ p) and does not establish that K(K φ → φ) is necessary.

judgement.summary: Target proves a valid and more general propositional modal theorem (∀ p, 𝓢 ⊢ ∼K(K(∼p) 🡘 p) from Def1–Def4), but it is divergent from [P-A4] because it cannot express Reinhardt's schema, Turing-machine indices W_e, or the quantified epistemic instantiation steps that link an instance of Reinhardt's schema to K(K(∼p) 🡘 p). Consequently, the Lean statement establishes something materially different from the source claim that an instance of Reinhardt's schema is inconsistent with epistemic arithmetic.
